thread:
Anya Patel: FYI I'm seeing a reproducible latency spike on multi-GPU runs after enabling CUDA graph replay. 3x tail latency on short sequences. Tensor+pipeline parallel, 8-way allreduce.
Mike Chen: What changed recently? model/kernel selection or batching heuristics?
Anya Patel: No model change; rolling back graph replay fixes it. KV-cache warmup looks normal. Example log from the failing run:
```
[runner] capture_start: graph_id=42
[nvtx] kernel: attention_fwd 8ms
[comm] allreduce enqueue behind stream 0x7f7b0c
[cuda-graph] replay: external stream detected; fallthrough
[runner] idle wait 32ms
```
Devon Rivera: That "external stream detected" line rings a bell — capture/replay + external streams can change ordering across captures. If allreduce is launched on a different stream and the graph replay reuses streams, we can lose comm/compute overlap.
Lee Wong: Can you paste the perf timeline (nvprof/nvtx) clipped around the spike? small ascii timeline is fine.
Anya Patel: pasted snippet:
```
NVTX: |---compute(12ms)---|   idle(28ms)   |---allreduce(9ms)---|
CUDA graph replay occurred at t+45ms, compute kernel re-launched inside graph, allreduce stayed on external NCCL stream and got serialized after replay restart.
```
Mike Chen: So compute got captured into the graph but the collectives stayed on an external stream -> replay reorders those relative to host-side enqueued events. That would remove overlap. Did we change stream capture flags? thread-local vs global?
Devon Rivera: Right. We likely need to either 1) capture the comm stream into the graph too, 2) avoid replay for sequences that trigger async allreduces, or 3) use cudaStreamAttachMemAsync/cudaGraphExecUpdate patterns. Capturing NCCL comm streams is sketchy across launches.
Lee Wong: I pushed a quick patch to mark capture as cudaStreamCaptureModeThreadLocal and to insert explicit cudaEventRecord before/after allreduce as a guard. Small run from my laptop shows idle reduced but allreduce still waits ~4ms longer.
Anya Patel: Ran Lee's patch on infra. Timeline after patch:
```
NVTX: |--compute(11ms)--|--graph-replay(0.5ms)--| idle(6ms) |--allreduce(13ms)--|
Total tail still +40% vs no-graph but much better than before.
```
infra-bot: deploy-bot: rollout 0.9.12 -> eng-runtime staging started by @Lee Wong
Mike Chen: Two angles: (A) runtime should detect NCCL/allreduce patterns during capture and refuse to reuse the graph across iterations that change comm/compute mapping, (B) improve kernel selection to favor fused kernels that reduce host enqueues so fewer external streams are used.
Devon Rivera: I'll add a small harness to reproduce minimal case (1 layer compute in graph + external NCCL on separate stream) and run with ASAN/TSAN to catch ordering violations. If reproducible we can add a fast path to serialize graph reuse when external comm detected.
Anya Patel: Thanks. For immediate mitigation, I'm going to flip graph-replay->no-replay for multi-GPU tests in CI and add a perf test that asserts comm/compute overlap > Xms. Leaving logs here: https://perf.redwood/tests/1955/graph-replay-spike
Mike Chen: Sounds good. Devon/Lee - please sync on patch and gate. I'll open a perf regression ticket and assign owners.
Devon Rivera: on it. I'll post reproducer in this thread once I have it compiled.
Anya Patel: thanks everyone :thumbsup:
